nodes.label: FinAlly AI Trading Workstation
nodes.rationale: Capstone for an agentic AI coding course; built entirely by coding agents that coordinate through planning/ files.

nodes.label: Single Container, Single Port Architecture
nodes.rationale: Students run one command; static Next.js export gives single origin with no CORS; single uvicorn worker so one in-memory price cache serves every SSE client.

nodes.label: SSE over WebSockets
nodes.rationale: One-way push is all that is needed; simpler, no bidirectional complexity, universal browser support.

nodes.label: Static Next.js Export
nodes.rationale: Single origin, no CORS issues, one port, one container.

nodes.label: SQLite Database with Startup Initialization
nodes.rationale: No auth means no multi-user, so no DB server needed; initialized in FastAPI lifespan because market source and startup snapshot need it; seeding only on first profile creation so deleted watchlist rows are not re-seeded.

nodes.label: Market Orders Only, Whole Shares
nodes.rationale: Eliminates order book, limit order logic and partial fills - dramatically simpler portfolio math.

nodes.label: Two Market Data Implementations, One Interface
Shared Price Cache
nodes.rationale: Single background task writes; SSE streams read; supports future multi-user without data-layer changes.

nodes.label: day_change_percent / reference_price Baseline
nodes.rationale: Simulator mode: first price since server start (seed); Massive mode: previous trading day close.

nodes.label: user_id Single Module-Level Constant
nodes.rationale: Kept in schema for future multi-user support without migration, but nothing built around it.

nodes.label: portfolio_snapshots table
nodes.rationale: Recorded at startup and after each trade only; no periodic task - frontend extends P&L line with live prices.

nodes.label: API Error Envelope and Error Codes
nodes.rationale: Single body shape {error:{code,message}} replaces FastAPI default; messages are user-displayable; unknown /api paths return JSON not_found.

nodes.label: Trade Rules Order (watched, priced, cash/shares)
nodes.rationale: Trades never add to the watchlist implicitly; fill at cached price at moment of execution.

nodes.label: DELETE /api/watchlist/{ticker}
nodes.rationale: Rejected with 409 position_open while a position is open so every held ticker always has a live price.

nodes.label: LLM Integration (LiteLLM -> OpenRouter -> Cerebras)
nodes.rationale: No token streaming - Cerebras inference is fast enough that a loading indicator suffices.

nodes.label: LLM Structured Output Schema (message, trades, watchlist_changes)
LLM Action Auto-Execution (fixed order)
nodes.rationale: No confirmation: fake money, fluid demo, demonstrates agentic AI. Order add -> trades -> removals lets one response add+buy or sell+remove; failures returned inline, no second LLM call.

nodes.label: LLM Mock Mode (LLM_MOCK=true)
nodes.rationale: Fast, free, reproducible E2E tests; development without API key; CI.

nodes.label: Environment Variables (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, MASSIVE_API_KEY, LLM_MOCK, DB_PATH, STATIC_DIR)
nodes.rationale: DB_PATH and STATIC_DIR omitted from .env.example because an empty value in --env-file would override the Dockerfile defaults.

nodes.label: Lightweight Charts (single charting library)
nodes.rationale: One charting library only; sparklines are hand-rolled SVG and heatmap a custom CSS/SVG treemap.

nodes.label: Browser-Only Chart/Sparkline History
nodes.rationale: No backend price-history buffer; page refresh empties charts.

nodes.label: Multi-Stage Dockerfile (Node 20 -> Python 3.12)
nodes.rationale: --timeout-graceful-shutdown 2 lets docker stop finish while an SSE connection is open.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Port Binding 127.0.0.1:8000
nodes.rationale: App has no authentication and spends the user's OpenRouter key.

nodes.label: Start/Stop Scripts (mac and Windows)
nodes.rationale: Thin and idempotent; only supported launch path; FINALLY_CONTAINER/VOLUME/PORT overrides for verification.

nodes.label: Playwright E2E Tests with docker-compose.test.yml
nodes.rationale: Separate compose file keeps browser dependencies out of the production image.
